title: Myths About World Religions
objective: After this level you can correct common misconceptions, like the idea that most Muslims are Arabs, using what you know about each tradition.
summary: Most Muslims live in the Asia-Pacific region, not the Arab world; Allah is the Arabic word for God; more Christians live in sub-Saharan Africa than in Europe. Many myths treat a faith as one voice.

cards.headline: Most Muslims are Arabs? Christianity is European? Every faith had a founder?
cards.body: All three are common beliefs, and all three are mistaken. Here's the evidence, and a habit for testing any claim about a religion.

cards.headline: Where Muslims live
cards.body: Picture the world's Muslims and many people picture the Arab world. But in 2020, about 59% of the world's Muslims lived in the Asia-Pacific region. Most Muslims, in other words, live outside the Middle East and North Africa.

cards.headline: Not every faith has a founder
cards.body: Many people assume every religion began with one founder. Not so. Hinduism has no single founder, no single scripture and no agreed set of teachings, as Level 41 showed. The Association of Shinto Shrines says Shinto has no founder, no dogma and no doctrine (Level 65). And Jains believe their teachings are eternal: Mahavira is the 24th and last Jina of this age, not their inventor (Level 48).

cards.headline: Christianity's new center
cards.body: Christianity is often pictured as a European faith. But in 2020, 30.7% of the world's Christians lived in sub-Saharan Africa, compared with 22.3% in Europe.

cards.headline: How to catch a myth
cards.body: Most myths about religion share one habit: they treat a faith as one voice. Remember Smart's point from Level 4: every tradition is a loosely held-together family of subtraditions. And Level 9's lesson: "unaffiliated" doesn't mean unbelieving. So before you trust an "all Muslims" or "all Christians" claim, ask: which ones, where, and who counted?

mascot.line: Mind the word: in Level 4, 'myth' meant a sacred story. Here it's the everyday kind, a claim that's simply mistaken.

cards.headline: Myths About World Religions: the takeaways
learned: Most Muslims live in the Asia-Pacific region
Not every faith has a founder
Myths usually treat a faith as one voice

questions.prompt: Match each group with its fact.
questions.explanation: In 2020 about 59% of Muslims lived in the Asia-Pacific region, and 30.7% of Christians lived in sub-Saharan Africa. Jains believe their teachings are eternal.

questions.prompt: A friend says every religion was started by one founder. Which example best corrects this?

options.label: Christianity, which traces back to Jesus
options.rationale: That is a tradition with a founder, so it fits the claim.

options.label: Sikhism, which began with Guru Nanak
options.rationale: Sikhism looks back to Guru Nanak, so it fits the claim.

options.label: Hinduism, which has no single founder
Islam, which Muslims trace to Muhammad
options.rationale: Muslims see Muhammad as the last prophet, so this does not correct the claim.

questions.explanation: Hinduism has no single founder, and Shinto and Jainism do not see themselves as founded either.

questions.prompt: Someone says "Christians all worship the same way." Which example from Level 4 best corrects this?

options.label: The Qafzeh burial with deer antlers
Smart's plain Baptist chapel and candlelit Orthodox church

questions.explanation: Smart's two churches, both Christian, worship very differently: every tradition is a family of subtraditions.
